classification.difficultyReason: Derive the vertical difference from three given heights, then use sine to find the inclined supporting arm.

content.prompt:
The pivot point ($P$) of the main supporting arm ($AP$) of a construction crane is 46 metres above the top of a 96-metre tall office building. When the supporting arm is at an angle of $55^\circ$ to the horizontal, the length of cable dropping from the point $A$ to the ground is 215 metres.

Find the length of the main supporting arm ($AP$), to the nearest centimetre.

spec.description: Unfilled office-building outline on the left, vertical support to P, arm rising right to A, vertical cable to the marked ground endpoint, and dashed horizontal reference from P to the cable. Decorative windows and building fill are omitted.
spec.mathematics: Roof height 96 m; pivot 46 m above the roof; cable height 215 m. The arm makes 55 degrees with the horizontal at P. The vertical rise from P to A is 73 m.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens appear; the derived rise and arm length are absent from the question diagram.

answer.worked:
The vertical rise from $P$ to $A$ is
$$\begin{align*}h &= 215-(96+46)\\&=73\ \mathrm{m}.\end{align*}$$
$$\begin{align*}\sin 55^\circ &= \frac{73}{AP}\\AP &= \frac{73}{\sin 55^\circ}\\AP &\approx 89.12\ \mathrm{m}.\end{align*}$$
